# parity-fuzz --mode expr baseline: normalized signatures of KNOWN gaps.
# A divergence whose signature is here is allowed; a NEW one fails CI.
# Regenerate: parity-fuzz --mode expr --count N --verify 3  (copy NEW-signature lines).
#
# SUBSTRING + TRAILING MODIFIER (fixed in subst.rs): the scalar-substring arm
# (gen_scalar_pe) now emits a `:MODIFIER` tail after `${var:OFF[:LEN]}` —
# `${v:0:8:h}` (substring then :h), `${v:2:h}` (offset-only + modifier, an alpha
# after the first colon is NOT a length per c:subst.c:1571), chains (`:h:t`), and
# bad letters (`:3`/`:Z`/`:x` → "unrecognized modifier `c'"). C applies the tail
# via modify() (c:3752-3792); the old naive `splitn(2, ':')` swallowed the third
# part as the length and failed with "bad math expression: ':' without '?'".
# Reverting the fix yields 10 divergences on seed 1. Bug #1014.
print -r -- "${(L#P)t}"
#
# (#) ON A BAD MATH EXPRESSION — the CI oracle predates the upstream fix.
# Upstream 0eab788437 ("52122 + 52129: fix (#) parameter expansion flag",
# 2023-09-13) rewrote substevalchar (c:Src/subst.c:1490). Before it:
#     zlong ires = mathevali(ptr);
#     if (errflag) return NULL;
# so a non-numeric operand made paramsubst return NULL, prefork bailed out of
# the word mid-expansion (c:Src/subst.c:142-147), and the node was left holding
# the still-tokenized source prefix — which untokenizes the Dnull back to a
# literal quote. Hence `print -r -- "${(#)path}"` emits a bare `"` and
# `echo a${(#):-@}z` emits `a`. After it:
#     if (errflag) { errflag |= saved_errflag; return noerrs ? dupstring("") : NULL; }
# i.e. an empty string whenever the (X) flag is absent, so the word survives.
# Test/D04parameter.ztst:2816 pins the new contract (`echo a${(#):-@}z` → `az`).
#
# zshrs ports the post-fix C, so it is the OLDER oracle that is out of step:
#     zsh 5.9   (Apple /bin/zsh, ubuntu 5.9-6ubuntu2)   a${(#):-@}z → "a
#     zsh 5.9.2 (Homebrew, zsh-5.9.2-0-gddee3e7)        a${(#):-@}z → az
#     zshrs                                             a${(#):-@}z → az
# `--mode expr --count 4000` against the 5.9.2 oracle reports 0 divergences with
# NO baseline at all; against a 5.9 oracle it reports exactly these two. Same
# fork-ahead-of-oracle split documented in zutil.txt and mathfunc.txt, and the
# same ruling as docs/BUGS.md #648 — matching the old oracle would mean
# re-introducing a bug upstream already deleted, so do NOT "fix" zshrs here.
# Retire these two lines once the ubuntu runner's zsh carries 0eab788437.
print -r -- "${(#)path}"
print -r -- "${(L#)path}"
